mechanism: Fit an AR model on close-to-close transition ratios (Levinson–Durbin), then run a discrete Kalman filter: Forecast multiplies prior state by the AR-predicted transition F and inflates P with process noise Q; Correction blends the new close z via Kalman gain. Treat corrected state above forecast as bullish and below as bearish; their cross is a trend-change signal. Two buffers (forecast red, correction blue) are non-repainting.
data_needed: Close series for symbol/TF; historyBars for AR (e.g. 3000); AR coeffs; Q=std of AR residuals; R=std of closes; recursive X,P,K.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; demo indicator on M30; EA test H1 August 2017; default PERIOD_H1; any symbol/TF via CKalman ctor.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a recursive state-space trend/change sensor that separates one-step predicted close from noise-corrected state, with explicit process vs measurement noise—stronger than a single MA cross.
quote: the blue line above the red one indicates a bullish trend. Conversely, the blue line below the red one is an indication of a bearish trend. The intersection of the blue and red lines is a trend change signal.

mechanism: Initialize measurement-noise covariance R as MathStandardDeviation of closes over the analysis window, and process-noise Q as MathStandardDeviation of the AR model’s reconstructed transition series. These enter the Kalman P update and gain, so the filter’s trust in prediction vs observation tracks local noise intensity.
data_needed: Close history window; AR residual series; std estimators for R and Q.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1/M30 as above; historyBars default 6240 in class ctor.
why_new_for_mis: Exposes dual noise covariances (observation vs process) as first-class volatility inputs to a state filter, usable as MIS vol features beyond ATR alone.
quote: For the calculation noise covariance, we use the root-mean-square value of deviations of Close values for the analyzed period.

mechanism: Author notes the Kalman EA loses in flat/sideways and suggests adding an explicit flat-movement filter (or time filter) before trusting the forecast/correction cross—i.e. Kalman trend sensor should be gated by a range regime detector.
data_needed: Kalman signal plus a flat detector (unspecified; suggested as future work).
why_new_for_mis: Documents that AR-Kalman direction sensing fails in range regimes, motivating a regime gate in MIS pipelines that use Kalman-like sensors.
quote: the strategy proposed and described in this article can become successful if supplemented with an additional filter for determining flat movements.

mechanism: Ralph Vince optimal-f sizing (HPR product max; Kelly; parametric normal; dual f1/f2 after win/loss) implemented as MQL5 Wizard money modules—position sizing, not market-state sensing. Z-score and serial correlation are diagnostics on the trade P&L stream for adjusting f, not price-regime sensors.
data_needed: Historical trade P&L array; max loss; optional win/loss streak stats.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic PL streams; Strategy Tester reports for any EA/symbol.
why_new_for_mis: After full read this is deposit/risk money-management only—no regime, vol, liquidity, or sequence market sensor.
quote: To find an optimal f value, we need to find the maximum of the product of all trades max(HPR1 * HPR2 * ... *HPRn).

mechanism: Open bidirectional virtual deals every bar, bin profit vs indicator value. Force Index (period 56, M5) shows a sharp profit collapse when rounded FI is in [-0.01, 0.01]; author attributes this to absence of volatility and forbids any entries in that band as a hard gate.
data_needed: iForce buffer; ATR for SL/TP; virtual deal outcomes; rounded FI step ~_Point*1000.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; analysis 2016-01-01 to 2017-10-01; Force on M5; also MACD M5, Chaikin/CCI D1; final EA test 2015–2017.
why_new_for_mis: Empirical profit-surface mining turns Force Index into a dead-zone volatility/liquidity-interest gate rather than a classical momentum oscillator signal.
quote: This observation may be explained by absence of volatility within the value range observed. For our strategy, make sure to mark prohibition to open any orders within this range.

mechanism: Technology of resolving entries into indicators: every bar open both long and short virtual deals with ATR-scaled SL/TP, record contemporaneous multi-TF indicator values, then plot profit vs indicator level (and vs 15:1 R:R for move force). Iteratively keep bands where empirical profit rises (e.g. MACD hist in [0.0015,0.0035] for buys) and add delta filters (Chaikin falling, CCI rising on D1).
data_needed: Virtual deal tickets; ADX/Alligator/CCI/Chaikin/Force/MACD on M5/H1/D1; ATR; profit/risk ratio runs.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; M5/H1/D1 indicators; test windows 2016–2017 then 2015–2017.
why_new_for_mis: MIS can treat indicator-conditioned expected-profit heat as a data-driven sensing layer that rediscovers usable bands without textbook signal lore.
quote: the technology for resolving entries into indicators implies comparison of open positions with indicator values.

mechanism: Catalog of 10 flat strategies that all couple a channel (Envelopes, BB, WSO/WRO, % crossover, Price Channel, WPR, Keltner, Donchian, ATR Channel, RSI hist) with an explicit flat/mode filter: MFI OB/OS, MA stack, Fractal Dimension Ehlers below threshold, TrendRange gray (flat>range), RBVI≤level, ADX<FlatLevel, Magic Trend unchanged (mt[0]==mt[1]), Trinity Impulse==0, CCI between color levels, Flat indicator < weak-trend level. Flat cues also include low trade interest / small tick volume / weak price change.
data_needed: Channel indicator buffers; flat-filter buffers (FDI, TrendRange, RBVI, ADX, MagicTrend, Trinity, CCI levels, Flat); close; H1 or lower TF for some.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; H1 for #1–2; any TF for most; Trinity strategy prefers M5–M30; tests last year, M1 OHLC.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a comparative menu of orthogonal flat-regime sensors (fractal dimension, RBVI, Trinity zero, MagicTrend freeze, ADX threshold) to gate range vs trend logic.
quote: Another sign of a flat period can be low volume of trades in the market or low interest from market participants. This can be seen from a weak price change, as well as from the small tick volume.

mechanism: Strategy #3 uses Fractal Dimension Ehlers (period 18, threshold 1.4) below threshold as confirmation that the market is not trending before taking WSO/WRO channel bounce entries—explicit market-mode sensing cited from Ehlers & Way.
data_needed: fdi buffer; wwc channel high/low; Inp_FdiThreshold.
why_new_for_mis: Fractal dimension as a dedicated trend/flat mode bit is a compact MIS regime feature distinct from ADX magnitude.
quote: To filter the signals, we will use the Fractal Dimension indicator, which was described in the article "Fractal Dimension as a Market Mode Sensor" by John F. Ehlers and Ric Way.

mechanism: RL agents learn buy/sell policy with Random Decision Forest. Features are Close[0]/Close[lag] increments over up to 500 lags; RecursiveElimination trains one-feature forests, ranks by OOB classification error, keeps bestfeatures_num lags, then retrains the forest. Monte Carlo random labeling during optimization explores policies; best model persisted by lowest OOB error. Multi-agent CRLAgents average signals across agents with different feature depths.
data_needed: Close vector (series); deal outcomes as labels; RDF trees, r regularization (train/OOB split); OOB error files.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Chart _Symbol; M15 Open-prices optimization ~2 months then forward months; multi-agent variant same.
why_new_for_mis: Turns lag-ratio price increments + OOB-selected RDF into a sequence classifier sensor with Monte Carlo model search—usable as an MIS neural/sequence regime-of-tradeability score.

mechanism: Reverse-martingale study finds that fixed clock-time entries (GBPUSD 15:15 and 19:45; EURUSD similar with August off) with tiny SL and huge TP work as a self-sufficient seasonal/session sensor; disabling Fridays and summer months further lifts expectancy—time-of-day and calendar filters as primary edge, indicators optional/harmful.
data_needed: Server time of bar; SL/TP points; optional weekday/month masks; reversing chain state.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD, GBPUSD; M15 main tests; once-a-day on M5; history ~1998–Jul 2018.
why_new_for_mis: Documents stable multi-decade clock-hour profitability islands as calendar/session sensing features independent of price indicators.
quote: Surprisingly, there are two time periods for GBPUSD, during which this trading system really works. These are 15:15 and 19:45.

mechanism: Reverse martingale (flip direction and double lot after SL, TP≥2×SL, max ~8 steps) tested with/without indicators; core contribution is risk/MM behavior, not a new price-state sensor.
data_needed: Open position; pending opposite stop at SL; lot multiplier.
why_new_for_mis: Primary article thrust is money-management reversing chains—not MIS market sensing (aside from the clock-time idea above).
quote: Reversing is a type of martingale.

mechanism: Combine trend strategy (ADX cloud + RSI color) with flat strategy (WPR + ADX flat level). Method 1: sequential signals, one position. Method 2: gate trend entries by flat_adx≥Flat_FlatLevel (require trend strength) and gate flat entries by flat_adx<Flat_FlatLevel plus RSI not opposing—ADX level is the regime switch between strategy blocks. Method 3: independent magics on hedge account.
data_needed: Trend ADX cloud + RSI buffers; flat WPR + ADX; Flat_FlatLevel (e.g. 40); separate SL/TP per block.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Optimized/tested ~2017-01-01 to 2018-01-08 then forward; symbol implied FX pair from prior articles (EURUSD context).
why_new_for_mis: Operationalizes ADX as a hard regime router that swaps which signal family is allowed—clean MIS pattern for multi-strategy orchestration.
quote: if there is a trend, use the trend-following algorithm, if there is no trend, use the flat one.

mechanism: Extends reversing with every-second-step lot doubling, broker-specific re-optimization, and broad tests on FX, stocks, ags, oil, indices, ETF. Findings are about MM risk and venue suitability (stocks/indices trend better for reversing), not a new sensing algorithm.
why_new_for_mis: After full read: risk/venue survey for reverse martingale—no new MIS price sensor (calendar sensing already captured from part 1).
quote: the stock market is perfect for applying reversing techniques.

mechanism: Short MetaQuotes promo that Freelance hit 50,000 completed orders; points to Code Base and Market—no sensing method.
why_new_for_mis: No MIS sensing content—service milestone announcement.
quote: Members of the official MetaTrader Freelance service have completed more than 50,000 orders as at October 2018.

mechanism: Build per-hour series of H1 close diffs at lag L; compute 24×24 correlation heatmap; clusters of high corr (e.g. hours 0–5 and 10–14 on EURUSD 2015–2020) mark seasonal co-moving session regimes. Mean of clustered hour increments can be negative/positive, biasing direction. Longer history (from 2000) thins correlations and can flip mean sign.
data_needed: H1 closes 2015–2020 (or 2000–2020); lag; corr threshold; hour masks.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; also M15 check with lag≈96.
why_new_for_mis: Session-hour correlation clusters are a structured intraday regime map MIS can use beyond crude London/NY flags.
quote: It is clear that the following clusters have the maximum correlation: 0-5 and 10-14 hours.

mechanism: For paired hours, predict next-hour increment via ret_pred = HF − (HF2 − HL2), i.e. Close[-1]=(Close[0]-Close[lag])-((Close[lag]-Close[lag*2])-(Close[lag-1]-Close[lag*2-1])); scatter real vs predicted; rfilter drops near-zero forecasts. EA sells in hours 10–14 when predicted move ≤ −threshold (mean bias negative 2015–2020). 3D plots show corr decays with hour distance (volatility clustering of nearby increments).
data_needed: Hour-filtered H1 diffs; lag (~17–30 optimal on H1); per-hour OpenThreshold; SL.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 primary; M15 forward lag ~100.
why_new_for_mis: Closed-form seasonal increment predictor from lagged same/nearby-hour memory—actionable MIS sequence/session sensor with explicit distance-decay structure.

mechanism: Cross-platform MT4/MT5 grid EA (BuyStops above, SellStops below, close all at $ takeProfit). Tests show both-side fill lockups; long-term simple grids not viable—implementation/engineering article, not a market sensor.
data_needed: Bid/ask; grid step; maxLimits; equity profit sum.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M5; Aug 2018–Jan 2019 then 5y; also discusses stop-per-order variants.
why_new_for_mis: No MIS sensing method—grid execution/MM experiment concluding naive grids fail long-term.
quote: Unfortunately, ideas based on simple griders are not viable.

mechanism: Remove MathAbs in ADX so the main line becomes a signed oscillator (ADX_Osc) tracking directional strength for classic/hidden divergence lines. Separately, when +DI and −DI move unidirectionally (both up or both down)—Price Action “inside-bar” / consolidation analogue on strength—plot arrows: with-trend ADX_Osc move → stop/consolidation points; against-trend → reversal-leaning points (green buy / purple sell; blue/gold mark uncertainty). Gap merges nearby points into a trail level; trade on close beyond the point, not pending.
data_needed: +DI/−DI/ADX buffers; high/low; extremum count; Gep points; optional divergence trendlines.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDJPY; H1 and H4; test 2016-01-01 to 2019-06-01.
why_new_for_mis: Converts lagging ADX into a signed strength oscillator plus a DI-unison micro-regime change sensor—actionable short-horizon stop/reverse cues beyond textbook DI crosses.
quote: Bulls power at the current bar is less than at the previous one, while Bears power is greater than at the previous bar. The bar shape is irrelevant.

mechanism: Reframe classic A/B/C divergence grades: treat divergence primarily as a stopping signal; a later confirmation decides whether price reverses or the trend resumes. Hidden/reverse divergence used with lines as S/R. Critiques MACD/Stoch/RSI/CCI/Momentum/volume tools for automation pitfalls; prefers multi-filter (e.g. RSI+ZigZag) and ADX_Osc implementation.
data_needed: Oscillator extrema vs price highs/lows; optional volume; confirmation structure.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex majors as above; multi-TF examples M5–H1 for Stoch; visual multi-indicator survey.
why_new_for_mis: Sensing taxonomy shift—MIS can emit stop-threat vs confirmed-reversal as two-stage change states instead of single divergence flags.
quote: The signal is essentially a stopping one. Then the confirmation signal can show whether the market will reverse or not.
